references.text: The prohibition against eating meat with blood in it dates back to the covenant with Noah after the flood.
An expanded prohibition against eating blood, with an explanation that blood contains the life force.
Reiterates the prohibition against eating blood because the blood is the life.
Prohibition against divination, sorcery, and witchcraft, parallel to the ban on practicing augury and fortune-telling.
Saul warns the people against eating meat with blood in it, showing practical application of this prohibition.
Manasseh practiced augury and witchcraft, which was a violation of this prohibition.
Manasseh practiced sorcery and witchcraft, parallel to the prohibitions in Leviticus.
The prophet Ezekiel rebukes Israel for eating meat with blood, violating this prohibition.
The Apostolic Council confirms the prohibition against eating blood for Gentile Christians.
The apostolic letter reiterates the ban on blood as one of the fundamental rules for Gentile Christians.
Sorcery (φαρμακεία) is mentioned as a work of the flesh, parallel to the ban on augury and divination.
